newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms have no sex harassment countermeasures.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms have no sex harassment countermeasures.

text.p: Most Japanese firms have not adopted specific measures to counter sexual harassment against female employees and few companies feel the need to do so in the future, a government survey issued on Thursday said.

The Management and Coordinating Agency's report on sexual harassment said 92.5 percent of 239 firms surveyed during April and June had adopted no countermeasures, such as counsellors and outside or neutral complaint handlers, to deal with sexual harassment cases.
Of those firms without such countermeasures, 75 percent replied they feel they do not need to adopt such measures in the future.
On the other hand, sexual harassment complaints were increasing, the agency survey said. Complaints have doubled from the 104 cases reported to prefectural offices in 1995 to 203 this year.

The agency survey also said many firms will not employ females because of the Labour Standard Law which bans firms from making women work after 10 p.m., except for a few jobs like doctors, nurses and broadcast announcers.
The Management and Coordinating Agency said it would soon announce a set of sexual harassment guidelines for firms and recommendations for the Labour Ministry to revise labour laws.
